title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
lede: Dario Amodei called claims that Anthropic would hand human free will to AI absurd, and proposed limits on recursive self-improvement even as Anthropic automates more of its own research.

points: In a long X post, Amodei said governance by AI is a bad idea for the same reasons he opposes autocracy.
He separates automating specific tasks, like driving, drug design or end-to-end software, from giving up human agency.
He suggested limits on recursive self-improvement and said Claude should not build successive frontier models without meaningful human supervision.
Claude wrote over 80% of code merged at Anthropic as of June, and METR found its models improving at about twice their historical rate.
He accused rivals of vibes-based positioning, noting every lab ships models built to automate ever more tasks.

sections.text: Developers building on Claude get a stated line from its maker: broad task automation is fine, but fully autonomous model development still needs human oversight.
